messages.text: Horner reveals Red Bull decision that helped Mercedes sign Hamilton

metadata.summary: Christian Horner has revealed he helped Mercedes sign Lewis Hamilton after holding early discussions with the British driver's management to join Red Bull.
metadata.content: Christian Horner reveals Red Bull talks with Lewis Hamilton management before telling Mercedes' Niki Lauda to sign British driver | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Christian Horner reveals Red Bull talks with Lewis Hamilton management before telling Mercedes' Niki Lauda to sign British driver Christian Horner joins Simon Lazenby on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show Podcast to reveal all on Red Bull talks with Lewis Hamilton before the latter joined Mercedes and his thoughts on Kimi Antonelli, who could become world champion this Sunday at the United States GP Wednesday 21 October 2026 06:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner jokes that Toto Wolff's life is much easier without him in F1, reflecting on their fierce rivalry over the years Christian Horner has revealed he helped Mercedes sign Lewis Hamilton after holding early discussions with the British driver's management to join Red Bull. Hamilton left McLaren to join Mercedes at the start of 2013 but in Horner's new book, 'Drive ', which will be on sale from this Thursday, he says Hamilton showed interest to join Red Bull. Senior figures at Red Bull, including co-owner Dietrich Mateschitz, were not keen on the move that would have seen Hamilton replace Mark Webber and become Sebastian Vettel's team-mate from 2013. messages.text: NBA season tips off as Detroit stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Celtics

metadata.summary: Detriot Pistons staged an epic 23-0 run in the fourth quarter as they overcame a 22-point deficit - the largest come-from-behind win against the Boston Celtics in the last 30 seasons - to seal a stunning 121-113 win.
metadata.content: NBA: Detroit Pistons stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Boston Celtics as season tips off in style | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NBA: Detroit Pistons stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Boston Celtics as season tips off in style Detroit Pistons rally from 22-points down to beat Boston Celtics 121-113 with Javonte Green and Cade Cunningham’s 22 points and 8 assists winning the day at Little Caesars Arena Tuesday 20 October 2026 23:19, UK Image: Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives on Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum (0) in the NBA season tip off Detriot Pistons staged an epic 23-0 run in the fourth quarter as they overcame a 22-point deficit - the largest come-from-behind win against the Boston Celtics in the last 30 seasons - to seal a stunning 121-113 win. Javonte Green scored 19 points after not playing in the first half and Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points and eight assists, helping the Pistons to victory as the NBA season tipped off in style on Tuesday. Paul George scored 38 points, the most by a Celtic in his debut. The nine-time All-Star, in his 17th season, showed he's still got it in his first game with Boston since it acquired him from Philadelphia in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown. messages.text: LeBron's Sixers knock off champion Knicks in sensational victory

metadata.summary: LeBron James got his Philadelphia 76ers career off to a sensational winning start as his side beat the reigning champion New York Knicks 106-100 at Madison Square Garden on NBA opening night.
metadata.content: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers knock off champion New York Knicks in sensational road victory to open NBA season | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers knock off champion New York Knicks in sensational road victory to open NBA season The Philadelphia 76ers beat the New York Knicks side 106-100 at Madison Square Garden in LeBron James' debut with his new team; James recorded 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists to complement standout performer Tyrese Maxey's 28-point haul Wednesday 21 October 2026 07:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA match between the New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers LeBron James got his Philadelphia 76ers career off to a sensational winning start as his side beat the reigning champion New York Knicks 106-100 at Madison Square Garden on NBA opening night. James began his NBA-record 24th season with 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists, while Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points and James' fellow Sixers debutant Jaylen Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists in his first game since being acquired from Boston. Jalen Brunson scored 21 points but the NBA Finals MVP shot just 6 for 19 from the field. metadata.summary: Como's rise has been remarkable, but the ambition is to make their success last.

Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Wednesday 21 October 2026 07:29, UK Como's rise has been remarkable, but the ambition is to make their success last. The club's journey from Italy's lower leagues to Serie A and Champions League qualification is an extraordinary story. Yet what makes it so compelling is the speed of their progress, combined with a determination to establish themselves as a force in Italian football for years to come. In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News , Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi reflects on the club's transformation, the influence of head coach Cesc Fabregas and an unlikely reunion with Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes.
